label: architect • paged issue digest with auth, per-issue decision, memory, and a report file
query:
Our issue tracker has an API at {{fixture.base_url}}. GET /v1/issues lists open issues two at a time as {"issues": [{"id", "title", "body"}], "next_cursor": "..."}. To get the next page, send next_cursor back as the `cursor` query parameter; next_cursor is null on the last page. Every request needs the header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. I have the token and will enter it when you ask.

Build me a workflow that goes through every open issue, decides for each one whether it is urgent (an outage, lost data, or a security problem), and makes a Markdown report file listing the urgent ones, each with its id and a one-line reason. It should remember which issues it has already looked at, so the next run only covers new ones. Test it, then offer to save it.
notes: Hard case. Three cursor pages behind bearer auth (401 without the token). Pins paginate on the http step, a declared secret read through `auth`, a per-issue decision (map + inference), a state step that remembers handled issues, and a Markdown file in the workflow output. The latest test's report names both urgent issues; a post-run after the Architect's tests must leave them out, because they were already seen.
